bounds: The 60 s grace is DELIBERATE: a settled row is still visible for up to a minute so the user can read its outcome. Clause 1's outcome is 'rows stop piling up', not 'a row vanishes the instant it finishes'.

ARM 2 correlates by NAME, and the host catalog's `description` for a team member is the member's DESCRIPTION (falling back to its NAME only when empty) — measured in packages/mpd-dsh-adapter-plugin/src/index.ts (`description: request.description === "" ? request.name : request.description`). So in production ARM 2 fires for a member with an empty description; other member rows burn through ARM 1 once their run is terminal, which still satisfies clause 1 for teams. This is a correlation BOUND, stated rather than papered over.

The burn projection is OPT-IN (no filter ⇒ unfiltered): the sidebar does not burn yet because panel-dag.ts is L2's write scope. L2's exact recipe is in evidence/tui/panel-wave/l4-row-lifecycle/signatures.md.
The team arm requires an exact, unambiguous name match; a description that merely CONTAINS a member name (e.g. "Member — task") does not fire and follows ARM 1.

MPD's consult records are an in-process Map in mpd-roles-plugin and are NOT readable from the TUI, so the rule cannot ask 'did MPD spawn this row?'; it is decided from the row itself plus the session's own team projection.

A row the channel read is session-scoped: the panel snapshot carries no per-row parent id, so its rows are this session's by construction; only a channel row that NAMES another parent session is protected from the burn.
